Simulate 2D natural convection in a square cavity using buoyantBoussinesqPimpleFoam.
The domain is a 1 m x 1 m square in the x-y plane, from (0, 0) to (1, 1).
The mesh is 41 x 41 cells in the x-y plane, with a single cell in the z-direction (1-cell-thick 2D slab).
The front and back faces (z-normal) use empty boundary conditions to enforce 2D behaviour in 3D OpenFOAM.
The fluid is air, with thermophysical properties evaluated at the reference temperature of 295 K.
Gravity is g = (0 -9.81 0) m/s².
The Boussinesq approximation is used for the buoyancy source term in the momentum equation, with the thermal expansion coefficient set to 1/T_ref where T_ref = 295 K.
The temperature boundary condition on the left wall (x = 0) is fixedValue 300 K.
The temperature boundary condition on the right wall (x = 1) is fixedValue 290 K.
The temperature boundary condition on the top wall (y = 1) is zeroGradient.
The temperature boundary condition on the bottom wall (y = 0) is zeroGradient.
The velocity boundary condition on all four walls is noSlip.
The pressure boundary condition on all four walls is zeroGradient.
Initial conditions: T = 295 K everywhere, U = (0 0 0) everywhere, p = 0 Pa everywhere.
The front and back faces carry no physical boundary conditions (empty for U, p, T, and all other fields).
Run the simulation in transient mode with a fixed or adaptive time step appropriate for the PIMPLE algorithm, and monitor the Nusselt number along the hot wall for validation against published data.
